coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Potrero Power Station Block 15 / Station A
record.summary: Adaptive reuse of the 1901-02 Station A turbine hall into an approximately 456,000 gsf office building with an eight-story vertical addition, approved by the Planning Director on March 2, 2022 (the Planning Commission granted its office allocation on October 22, 2020); as of the 2024 annual compliance report, construction of the addition had not started (only 2024 brick stabilization work is described). In a request reported July 29, 2026, the developer asked to raise Station A's height by 30 feet; the Planning Commission approved the amendment unanimously (reported Aug 3, 2026) and the Board of Supervisors passed the amended development agreement on first reading on Sept 29, 2026, and Legistar lists it as approved by the Mayor and enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Enactment Nos. 208-26 and 209-26 for the agreement and its zoning ordinance); the enacted height map gives 175 ft on the northern half and 190 ft on the southern half (145 and 160 ft in the adopted rules), taking effect Nov 13, 2026 by our count.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is Assessor lot 4175026, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. That this is the lot of Block 15 (Station A) is Pier & Point's own inference from location, shape and size (our earlier trace of the D4D figure measured 5,104 m2 against the lot's 4,315 m2; 85% of the trace lies inside the lot and the trace covers 100% of it). No Port document read ties the lot number to it. A building may sit back from the lot lines. Block 15 is Station A, an existing historic building (the 1901 turbine hall; DBI permit 202406053802 in 2024 describes the unoccupied 'station a building'), so it is not vacant land; the approved vertical addition has not been started.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lot 4175026 (recorded 2022-08-30; mapped 2023-12-01; active); cross-checked against Potrero Power Station Design for Development Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (printed p.245, PDF p.247).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: No single Assessor lot is documented as Block 15 (Station A). Lot 4175026 (active) matches its location, shape and size, so its outline is Assessor lot 4175026; the identification is Pier & Point's inference, as the accuracy note says.
notes.regulatory_context: Station A: the site's historic 1901 unreinforced-brick turbine hall (a four-story brick structure per the 2018 Draft EIR), vacant/unoccupied. The design review approves adaptive reuse into approximately 403,750 GSF of office (the Planning Commission granted the office allocation on Oct 22, 2020, Motion 20801) via an eight-story vertical addition above the retained historic shell and a public mid-block passage through the building (the design-review memo describes it as accessible from both Georgia Lane and Power Station Park in one place, and as connecting Georgia Lane and Louisiana Paseo in another), designed by Herzog & de Meuron with Adamson Associates; the Planning Director approved the Design Review Application on March 2, 2022. The design-review memo gives a total height of 205 feet measured from grade for the Station A building with its eight-story addition, but also says the addition is 'subject to the prevailing 145-foot and 160-foot building height maximums', and the D4D's Figure 6.2.3 labels the block's two strips 145' and 160'; the sources read do not reconcile the two figures. The Chronicle (July 29, 2026) reports a requested Development Agreement amendment that would let Station A grow by 30 feet; it is not shown here as enacted. Construction of the addition had not started per SF YIMBY (Aug 27, 2025) and the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025), which describes only 2024 brick stabilization work. The 2018 Draft EIR project proposed demolishing Station A (its Alternative D retained it); SF YIMBY (June 2021) says the adaptive reuse was included following community pushback against demolition, and no source found names who advocated for it.

open_questions: No construction-start date for the vertical addition is stated in any source found; the most recent primary source found (the 2024 annual compliance report, submitted March 2025) describes design approval and 2024 brick stabilization work, not adaptive-reuse construction. The Oct 22, 2020 Planning Commission minutes were not found at a checkable URL; the Design Review Approval memo is cited for that hearing instead.

The 2022 design review approval describes a 205-ft total height for the Station A addition, while the adopted D4D (section 6.14.5) allows new construction on Station A up to 145 feet on the northern half and 160 feet on the southern half; how the 205 ft relates to those limits (for example whether it includes the existing walls or rooftop elements) is not stated in the sources read. The '230'MAX' label in the D4D's Figure 6.2.3, which also appears on the enacted map along the southern strip, is a dimension marker, not a height.

The Chronicle's July 2026 report of a proposed +30 ft height increase for Station A is tied to the Development Agreement amendment (BOS File 260724) and Planning Code ordinance (File 260770), which passed the Board of Supervisors on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 and finally on Oct 6, 2026 (11 ayes), and Legistar lists it enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Legistar: Mayor 'APPROVED'; enactment numbers 208-26 and 209-26; page read Oct 14, 2026). The enacted height map labels the strips "175'" and "190'" (File 260770 'Leg Final' attachment, p. 29), 30 ft above the adopted 145 and 160, effective November 13, 2026 by our count (a legal date computed by Pier & Point, not printed in the text). Whether the 2022 design review approval (205 ft total) is affected by the new limits is not stated in the sources read.
No source found stating a cost estimate for Station A's rehabilitation and vertical addition.

The Draft EIR image shown here as a 'before' view is not a single photograph -- it is a composite DEIR report page carrying six separate existing-conditions photos of Station A's turbine hall and machine shop, each with its own caption. It may be better described as a document than as a single before photo.

The February 17, 2020 photo is shown as a current ('now') view rather than a 'before' view because the most recent primary source found (the 2024 annual compliance report, submitted March 2025) describes no adaptive-reuse construction on Station A (only 2024 brick stabilization), so the building's exterior likely hasn't changed much since. If construction has started since 2026-09-24, this photo is out of date.

Corrected 2026-10-06 (accuracy audit, October 2026): the July 2026 Development Agreement amendment request was shown as an expected event after it had been made and heard; it is now shown as having happened, with the Planning Commission's unanimous approval (SF Standard, August 3, 2026). Update 2026-10-12: the Board of Supervisors passed the amendment package on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 (see milestones). Update 2026-10-17: Legistar lists the package as approved by the Mayor and enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Enactment Nos. 208-26 and 209-26; page read Oct 17, 2026); the Board's final passage on Oct 6, 2026 (Ayes: 11) is shown by the Clerk of the Board's certificate in each file's 'Leg Final' attachment (File 260724 attachment pp. 11-12; File 260770 attachment pp. 58-59), although the Legistar web page's 10/6/2026 history row carries no action text.

Story count of Station A: the 2022 Design Review Approval (March 2, 2022) describes the existing Station A plus an 8-story vertical addition; SF YIMBY (June 2021) called it a twelve-story adaptive reuse.
